flavor: Every war ends, the treaties promise. The deep has kept count, and it has room for a few more.
rules: Any named war, ancient or modern, legendary ones like the Trojan War included: civil wars, wars of independence and long rebellions all count. Battles, sieges, risings put down within weeks and wars of gods or fiction don't.

answers.lore: Britain and Iceland clashed three times over fishing grounds between 1958 and 1976. Iceland got its way each time.

answers.lore: A war of 1778 and 1779 with almost no battles. Armies spent it foraging, hence its nickname: the Potato War.
In 1838 France blockaded Mexico, in part over a French pastry cook's shop that had been looted in Mexico City.
Ohio and Michigan raised militias over Toledo in 1835. Only one man was hurt, and Michigan got the Upper Peninsula instead.
In 1925 a Greek soldier is said to have chased his dog over the Bulgarian border and been shot. Greece invaded, briefly.
France and Brazil sent warships over lobster fishing in the 1960s. The argument: does a lobster swim, or walk on the seabed?
The last phase of the war between Chad and Libya, in 1987, named after the Toyota pickups that carried Chad's troops.

answers.lore: In 1859 an American farmer shot a British-owned pig on San Juan Island. Britain and the US held the island jointly until 1872. The pig was the only casualty.

answers.lore: In 1784 the Dutch fired a single shot at an Austrian ship. It hit a soup kettle, and that was the war.
Legend says the war of 1325 began when soldiers of Modena stole a bucket from a well in Bologna. Modena still has the bucket.
For decades Canada and Denmark fought over tiny Hans Island by leaving each other bottles of whisky and schnapps. They split it in 2022.
